justification: Checkout page in English with html lang="en" — language attribute matches content; transparent itemized pricing ($129+$19=$148), disabled place-order until T&C accepted, no hidden fees or misleading elements.
Explicitly labeled 'Deterministic'; refresh always yields the same outcome, no fake loading states, no bait-and-switch content. Honest design.
Newsletter opt-in with neutral yes/no buttons ('Yes, claim my 10% discount' / 'No, thanks') of equal visual weight; no shaming or guilt language; real button element for the decline path.
Fixed 4-section feed; footer with legal links statically reachable (distance 0px, never mutated on scroll). No endless-scroll or hidden opt-out.

Decline option styled as near-invisible 9px grey text at 1.6:1 contrast ('No, I'll just keep reading ads') while the trial button is a large bold rose CTA; exit path visually buried — confirmshaming/visual hierarchy manipulation.

Variable-ratio reinforcement design: labeled 'Variable-ratio', copy promises 'some pulls... surprise you' and 'will this be the one that pays off?' — an intermittent-reward schedule engineered to hook users into compulsive refreshing, like a slot machine.
Plain account settings page; delete-account is clearly marked in a 'Danger zone' with an explicit irreversible-action warning and visible button. No friction asymmetry or hidden paths.
Invite/skip choice presented fairly: both buttons same size, skip option clearly available, copy explicitly says 'Your choice, either way'. No pressure to grant contact access.

Fabricated endorsements: all three 'Verified Purchase' reviews are templated stock-photo avatars with near-identical text ('Absolutely love it!'), and the provenance check reveals similarity ~1.00, 1/3 unique avatars — fake reviews presented as authentic customer testimonials.
Data-processing notice written in plain, readable English (FKGL 10.5, below grade-9 threshold); explicit confirmation checkbox; transparent and honest consent flow.

Account-deletion dialog weaponizes coercive copy: 'FINAL', 'GONE FOREVER', 'you will REGRET it', 'your friends will MISS you', a deliberately unreadable legal sentence, and the jab 'who has time for that?' — emotional coercion to block a legitimate exit.
Paywall offers 'Start 7-day free trial' vs 'No, thanks — continue for free'; both buttons equal size, weight and contrast, no shaming or guilt language. Fair choice.
Fake demand pressure: '128 people are viewing this' / '128 watching now' with an animated icon and no temporal or geographic qualifier — an unfalsifiable scarcity claim designed to rush the purchase.

Cookie banner in English but the opt-out control 'Refuser les cookies non essentiels' is rendered in French while the accept button is in English — the refusal path is hidden behind a language barrier, manufacturing consent for the default.
Cookie banner fully in the user's language (en-US): both 'Accept all cookies' and 'Reject non-essential cookies' in clear English; no linguistic asymmetry.

Coercive ad escalation: 'Ad length grows the longer you stay free' — pre-roll ads inflate 5s→10s→15s as the user resists paying, deliberately worsening the free experience to push a purchase ('pay to avoid').
Account deletion presented with neutral, factual copy: clear consequences, data-export option, refund statement, equal-weight Delete/Keep buttons, 'no pressure, no guilt'. Respectful design.
Static, truthful stock indicator ('In stock — 8 units', never flickers); no countdown, no fabricated scarcity — explicitly 'No churn, no pressure'.

Checkout page is in English (lang="en", English order summary and Place-order button) but the legal consent controls — 'Términos y Condiciones' and 'Acepto los Términos y Condiciones y la Política de Privacidad' — are in Spanish, so the user can't read what they're agreeing to. The critical consent node is in a mismatched language.

Progress bar overstates reward progress by 2x (actual 10% after 2/10 ads but bar fills to 20%, growing 10% per ad vs real 5%) — a misleading progress indicator that keeps users watching more ads than the bar suggests.

Intermediate currency hides true cost: item priced in 1,299 coins; clicking 'Buy' routes to a coin store (no fiat gateway presented), forcing a $47.10 purchase for a $40.79-equivalent item and stranding 201 unusable coins — decoupling perceived price from real spend.

Decline option is a <span> (not a button, no role=button), unreachable by keyboard and unannounced to screen readers, and framed as 'No, thanks — I'll pay full price' — structurally degraded exit plus loss-framing to push the opt-in.

Marketing-consent checkbox in plain English ('I agree to receive marketing communications... I can unsubscribe at any time'), zero negations, checked=opt-in clearly stated; trial terms ($0/30 days, auto-renews) disclosed upfront. Honest wording.
Video playback starts automatically with no user intent ('You never pressed play', intent = none) — unsolicited auto-play consumes data/attention and is a known manipulative default.

Consent checkbox worded with 15 negations ('I do not decline to not receive marketing communications...') whose plain meaning is 'I agree to receive marketing communications' — deliberately unreadable double-negative trick question that reverses its own meaning.
Price shown directly in fiat (PLN 149.00/year, VAT incl.) with an explicit conversion to USD/EUR defined in the DOM — fully comparable across markets, no price obfuscation.
Video is opt-in: labeled 'opt-in', playback starts only after the user presses 'Press to play'. No unsolicited autoplay.
Direct fiat checkout — $40.79 charged straight to the card; no coin top-up, no exchange rate, no intermediate currency interposed.

'Delete account' is styled identically to 'Save changes' (same rose button, same weight, 8px apart) with no confirmation step — a destructive action disguised as a routine one, engineered for accidental clicks.

Footer 'keeps moving': the DOM is mutated to push the footer down as the user scrolls ('approaching footer — DOM mutated, footer pushed down'), and the legal links (Privacy Policy etc.) are non-interactive <span> elements — infinite-scroll hides legal content and blocks opt-out access.

Reviews from distinct profiles (MK/AB/RW) with unique avatars (3/3) and non-templated texts (similarity 0.14); provenance check confirms authentic endorsements.
Demand claim is bounded and falsifiable ('128 people viewed this in the last hour' — temporal qualifier present, checkable against analytics). No fake urgency.
